MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which number is written in words as "six thousand and forty-five"? (1 mark)
   A. 645
   B. 6,405
   C. 60,405
   D. 6,045

2. How many factors does 12 have? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 6
   C. 8
   D. 5

3. Which statement about 486 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is neither even nor odd
   B. It is even because it ends in 6
   C. It is odd because it ends in 6
   D. It is odd because it has an even number of digits

4. Which statement about 7,351 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is neither even nor odd
   B. It is even because it has an odd number of digits
   C. It is odd because it ends in 1
   D. It is even because it ends in 1

5. What is the total value of the digit 5 in 7,250? (1 mark)
   A. 50
   B. 5
   C. 10
   D. 500

6. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 3,425 + 2,318? (1 mark)
   A. 0
   B. 1
   C. 3
   D. 2

7. Work out 8,421 − 6,537. (1 mark)
   A. 1,784
   B. 2,116
   C. 1,894
   D. 1,884

8. Work out 43 × 12. (1 mark)
   A. 129
   B. 516
   C. 526
   D. 506

9. What is 95 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 23 remainder 4
   B. 24 remainder 3
   C. 22 remainder 7
   D. 23 remainder 3

10. What is 56 ÷ 8? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 17
   C. 6
   D. 7

11. What is 83 ÷ 9? (1 mark)
   A. 10 remainder 2
   B. 9 remainder 2
   C. 9 remainder 3
   D. 8 remainder 11

12. What is 300 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 300
   C. 3
   D. 30

13. What is 500 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 500
   C. 6
   D. 50

14. What is 4/9 of 27? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 3
   C. 13
   D. 15

15. Change 2 1/3 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 7/3
   B. 6/3
   C. 3/3
   D. 8/3

16. Write 2 3/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 2.03
   B. 23.0
   C. 0.23
   D. 2.3

17. Which is the largest number: 0.7, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57? (1 mark)
   A. 0.75
   B. 0.57
   C. 0.07
   D. 0.7

18. Write 0.6 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 6/100
   B. 6/10
   C. 1/6
   D. 60/10

19. Which price is the cheapest: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8.25
   B. Ksh 8.05
   C. Ksh 7.99
   D. Ksh 8.50

20. Write 0.05 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5/100
   B. 5/10
   C. 50/100
   D. 5/1000

21. Simplify 5x + 3y − 2x + y. (1 mark)
   A. 3x + 4y
   B. 7x + 4y
   C. 3x + 2y
   D. 7xy

22. Which expression shows "the sum of a and 9"? (1 mark)
   A. a − 9
   B. 9a
   C. a + 9
   D. a ÷ 9

23. What is 6 m 15 cm − 2 m 50 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 75 cm
   B. 3 m 55 cm
   C. 3 m 65 cm
   D. 4 m 65 cm

24. A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 26 cm
   B. 13 cm
   C. 28 cm
   D. 36 cm

25. What is 250 cm in metres? (1 mark)
   A. 25 m
   B. 0.25 m
   C. 2.5 m
   D. 2.05 m

26. Change 640 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 40 cm
   B. 6 m 90 cm
   C. 7 m 40 cm
   D. 64 cm

27. A square is covered with 6 rows of 6 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 24 square units
   B. 36 square units
   C. 42 square units
   D. 12 square units

28. One layer of a cuboid has 15 blocks and there are 3 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 42 blocks
   B. 18 blocks
   C. 60 blocks
   D. 45 blocks

29. Cuboid A is 4 by 3 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 3 by 3 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. Cuboid B
   C. Cuboid A
   D. It cannot be told

30. What is 5 1/2 L − 3 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/4 L
   B. 2 1/2 L
   C. 2 3/4 L
   D. 2 L

31. A goat has a mass of 32 kg and a sheep 27 kg. How much heavier is the goat? (1 mark)
   A. 4 kg
   B. 59 kg
   C. 6 kg
   D. 5 kg

32. What is 3 1/2 kg + 1 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5 kg
   B. 4 1/2 kg
   C. 4 3/4 kg
   D. 5 1/4 kg

33. Achieng buys 3 packets of flour of 1/2 kg each and 2 packets of sugar of 1 kg each. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 5 kg
   B. 2 1/2 kg
   C. 3 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

34. What is 6 kg − 2 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 4 kg
   C. 4 1/4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

35. What is 7 h 15 min − 3 h 50 min? (1 mark)
   A. 4 h 25 min
   B. 3 h 35 min
   C. 3 h 15 min
   D. 3 h 25 min

36. School ends at a quarter past three in the afternoon. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 3:45 p.m.
   B. 15:3 p.m.
   C. 3:15 a.m.
   D. 3:15 p.m.

37. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 2 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 3. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 2:15
   B. 2:03
   C. 3:15
   D. 2:45

38. A customer pays with Ksh 1,000 for goods that cost Ksh 865. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 125
   B. Ksh 1,865
   C. Ksh 135
   D. Ksh 235

39. How many corners does a triangle have? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 2
   C. 4
   D. 5

40. How many lines of symmetry does an oval have? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 2
   C. 0
   D. 1

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why 0.5 is greater than 0.45 even though 0.45 has more digits. (3 marks)

42. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact answer. (4 marks)

43. A garden bed has 9 rows and 4 columns of 1 m squares. Find its area in square metres. (2 marks)

44. Add 6,478 and 2,355 and check by estimating to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

45. Explain why the digit carried from the tens column must be added in the hundreds column when adding 3,568 + 2,276. (3 marks)

46. Write the decimal 5.68 in a place value chart and say the place value of the 6 and of the 8. (4 marks)

47. A triangle has two equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have? Explain how you can check. (3 marks)

48. Subtract 2 hours 35 minutes from 5 hours 20 minutes. (3 marks)

49. Write three reasons why we prepare a shopping list. (3 marks)

50. The table shows mango 4, banana 3, orange 2 and pawpaw 1. How many pupils did not choose mango? (2 marks)

51. A shopkeeper counts up to give change. A customer buys goods for Ksh 750 and pays with Ksh 1,000. Show how the shopkeeper counts up. (3 marks)

52. Work out 48 × 21 and check the answer by estimating first. (4 marks)

53. A tailor has 3 m 60 cm of cloth and uses 1 m 85 cm. How much cloth is left? (3 marks)

54. Otieno is a years old and his sister is 3 years older. Write an expression for his sister's age and find her age if Otieno is 9. (3 marks)

55. Nanjala says an angle with longer arms is always bigger. Is she right? Explain. (3 marks)

56. Two runners finish a race in 12.4 seconds and 12.35 seconds. Who is faster? Explain. (3 marks)

57. Njoki has 9 halves of oranges. How many whole oranges is that? Write your answer as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

58. Explain how multiplication can be used to check that 72 ÷ 6 = 12. (3 marks)

59. Write 4,605 in words and 305 in words. Then say which is greater. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 6,045
   six thousand and forty-five: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 6,045.

2. B — 6
   The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. There are 6 of them.

3. B — It is even because it ends in 6
   Look at the ones digit. 6 is even, so 486 is even.

4. C — It is odd because it ends in 1
   Look at the ones digit. 1 is odd, so 7,351 is odd.

5. A — 50
   The digit 5 is in the tens place, so its total value is 5 × 10 = 50.

6. B — 1
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 3,425 + 2,318 needs 1 regrouping.

7. D — 1,884
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 8,421 − 6,537 = 1,884. Check: 1,884 + 6,537 = 8,421.

8. B — 516
   43 × 2 = 86 and 43 × 10 = 430. 86 + 430 = 516.

9. D — 23 remainder 3
   4 × 23 = 92 and 95 − 92 = 3. So 95 ÷ 4 = 23 remainder 3. Check: 23 × 4 + 3 = 95.

10. D — 7
   8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7.

11. B — 9 remainder 2
   9 × 9 = 81 and 83 − 81 = 2. So 83 ÷ 9 = 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 9 + 2 = 83.

12. C — 3
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 300 ÷ 100 = 3.

13. A — 5
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 500 ÷ 100 = 5.

14. A — 12
   27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 3 × 4 = 12. So 4/9 of 27 is 12.

15. A — 7/3
   2 × 3 = 6 and 6 + 1 = 7. The denominator stays 3, so the answer is 7/3.

16. D — 2.3
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 2 3/10 = 2.3.

17. A — 0.75
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 0.75.

18. B — 6/10
   The last digit of 0.6 is in the tenths place, so the denominator is 10. 0.6 = 6/10.

19. C — Ksh 7.99
   Compare the shillings first. 7 is less than 8, so Ksh 7.99 is the smallest.

20. A — 5/100
   The last digit of 0.05 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.05 = 5/100.

21. A — 3x + 4y
   Only like terms can be joined. 5x + 3y − 2x + y = 3x + 4y.

22. C — a + 9
   The key words tell us the operation. "the sum of a and 9" is written a + 9.

23. C — 3 m 65 cm
   615 − 250 = 365 cm = 3 m 65 cm.

24. A — 26 cm
   Perimeter = 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm.

25. C — 2.5 m
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 250 cm in metres is 2.5 m.

26. A — 6 m 40 cm
   640 ÷ 100 = 6 remainder 40. So 640 cm = 6 m 40 cm.

27. B — 36 square units
   Area = 6 × 6 = 36 square units.

28. D — 45 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 15 × 3 = 45 blocks.

29. B — Cuboid B
   A = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 blocks. B = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

30. A — 2 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 1/2 L − 3 1/4 L = 2 1/4 L.

31. D — 5 kg
   32 − 27 = 5 kg.

32. C — 4 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 1/2 kg + 1 1/4 kg = 4 3/4 kg.

33. D — 3 1/2 kg
   3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 kg and 2 × 1 = 2 kg. 1 1/2 + 2 = 3 1/2 kg.

34. A — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 6 kg − 2 1/4 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

35. D — 3 h 25 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 3 h 25 min.

36. D — 3:15 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 3:15 p.m..

37. A — 2:15
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 3 shows 3 × 5 = 15 minutes, so the time is 2:15.

38. C — Ksh 135
   Change = amount paid − cost = 1,000 − 865 = Ksh 135.

39. A — 3
   A triangle has three sides and three corners.

40. B — 2
   An oval folds along its length and across its width.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.5 = 0.50. Comparing tenths, 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths, so 0.50 is greater than 0.45. The number of digits does not decide the size.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 0.5 as 0.50, 1 mark for comparing tenths, 1 mark for the conclusion.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280. Exact: 5,287.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for 5,280, 1 mark for 5,287.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: 36 square metres
   Working / marking points: 9 × 4 = 36. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for the unit.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Exact 8,833. Estimate 6,480 + 2,360 = 8,840, which is close.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact sum with regrouping, 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for the estimate.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ten tens make one hundred, so the extra 1 hundred must be counted with the hundreds. If it is left out the answer will be 100 too small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying ten tens make a hundred, 1 mark for the carried digit being added in the next column, 1 mark for the effect of leaving it out.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ones 5, tenths 6, hundredths 8. The 6 is in the tenths place and the 8 is in the hundredths place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct chart, 1 mark for each place value, 1 mark for using the decimal point correctly.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: One line of symmetry. Fold it from the top corner to the middle of the base and the two halves match.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for one, 1 mark for the fold, 1 mark for the halves matching.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: Change 5 h 20 min to 4 h 80 min (1 mark); 80 − 35 = 45 min (1 mark); 4 − 2 = 2 h, so 2 h 45 min (1 mark).

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: To remember everything we need; to buy only what is needed; to avoid spending more than we have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason, up to 3 marks.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils
   Working / marking points: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils; 10 − 4 = 6 (1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the answer).

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: From 750 to 800 is 50, and from 800 to 1,000 is 200. Change = 50 + 200 = Ksh 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for counting to 800, 1 mark for counting to 1,000, 1 mark for adding to make Ksh 250.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 50 × 20 = 1,000. Exact: 48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960, so 1,008.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for each partial product and 1 mark for the sum 1,008.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 75 cm
   Working / marking points: 360 − 185 = 175 cm (2 marks); 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm (1 mark).

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: a + 3. When a = 9, her age is 12 years.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a + 3, 1 mark for replacing a by 9, 1 mark for 12 years.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: No. The size of an angle depends on how far apart the arms are, not on how long they are.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no, 1 mark for the opening between the arms, 1 mark for length not mattering.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: The runner with 12.35 seconds is faster. 12.4 = 12.40, and 12.35 is less than 12.40, so it took less time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 12.4 as 12.40, 1 mark for comparing, 1 mark for the correct runner.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/2 oranges
   Working / marking points: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1 (2 marks); 4 1/2 (1 mark).

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Multiply the answer by the divisor: 12 × 6 = 72. This gives the starting number, so the division is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for multiplying the answer by the divisor, 1 mark for 12 × 6 = 72, 1 mark for the conclusion.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4,605 is four thousand, six hundred and five. 305 is three hundred and five. 4,605 is greater.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct wording and 1 mark each for the comparison and its reason (more digits).
